newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish ex-communists red-faced over election song.
newsitem.headline: Polish ex-communists red-faced over election song.

text.p: Poland's ruling ex-communists are embarrassed over a song they used to launch their election campaign -- the tune sounds remarkably like a number by Australian band Men at Work and the copyright owners are crying foul.
Artur Pacula of Sony Music, Polish representatives of Sony Music International, said he had heard reports that the melody resembled that of the band's song "Down Under".

"If this proves to be true, we will now wait for the opinion of our lawyers, and see what happens next," Pacula said, adding that the Social Democrats had not applied for permission to use the melody.

Leaders of the ruling Democratic Left Alliance (SLD) swayed and danced to the catchy number in front of television cameras on Sunday, smiling broadly at lyrics which proclaimed: "It will not be bad, together once again, naturally with the SLD".
Dariusz Klimaczewski, spokesman for the ruling Social Democrats, said that, if there were any doubts about the song, it would not be used in the campaign.
